title: Songbook and Tide
premise: Wren Zhou has spent five years hiding in her late grandmother's bookshop, raising her daughter alone and never telling the child's father, Theo Marsh, that she exists. When a snowstorm traps Wren, Theo, and his business rival—and Wren's old best friend—Priya Anand inside the shop overnight, the truth about her daughter surfaces, forcing all three to confront the betrayal that scattered them a decade ago. As the storm clears, Theo must choose between the coastal development deal Priya's firm is brokering—a deal that would demolish the bookshop block—and the family he never knew he had. In the end, Wren forgives herself for running, Theo walks away from the deal, and the three begin the slow, honest work of building something none of them planned.
about_author: Wren Halloran grew up in a seaside town where the library was the only building with good heating, and it shows. She writes love stories about people who stay too long in the wrong silences, from a drafty apartment overlooking a harbor.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the eve of the bookshop's fifth anniversary under her care, Wren navigates a normal day with her daughter Junie—school run, story hour, locked doors at dusk—while dodging news of a redevelopment proposal threatening the block. A flashback reveals she left town pregnant and unseen. Emotional beat: the ache of safety built on avoidance.

chapters.title: What the Storm Locks In
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, shifting to alternating perspectives as the blizzard hits. Theo arrives seeking her signature on relocation papers; Priya follows him in, their rivalry crackling. The power fails, candles come out, and Junie wanders downstairs calling a stranger 'Daddy' because he looks like her. Emotional beat: the past arriving all at once, unavoidable and lit by candlelight.

chapters.title: Every Truth Has a Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Through the long night, confessions surface: why Wren fled, why Priya let her believe the worst, why Theo signed away his music career for the deal now aimed at the shop. Priya admits she buried Wren's letters out of jealousy. At dawn, Theo learns Junie is his daughter and reels between fury and wonder. Emotional beat: betrayal laid bare, love refusing to leave.

chapters.title: A Song for Staying
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging on Wren. With roads cleared, Theo must sign the deal by noon or lose everything he built—but he tears up the contract instead, proposing instead to help save the block with Priya's reluctant pivot to preservation. Wren, finally forgiving the girl who ran, opens the shop door wide. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not what we're given, but what we choose to keep.
